about_the_game:
Fantasy platformer puzzle game.

Use the power of the elements to solve puzzles, interact with the world around you and unravel mysteries!

Platformer Mechanics about "Elements"

  • In this game, interacting with different elemental fields using various elemental slimes is a key mechanic.

  • There are five elemental fields: Water, Air, Fire, Lightning, and Earth. Each affecting different slimes in unique ways.

Example: Water Field

Each slime form interacts with the water field differently:

Water Slime → Can move freely in water, allowing smooth navigation.

Regular Slime → Water lifts you up, providing momentum to reach otherwise inaccessible platforms.

Earth Slime → Sinks rapidly, using the momentum to break special objects.

Lightning Slime → Electrifies the water, activating nearby gadgets, doors, or mechanisms.

Mastering these interactions is crucial for solving puzzles, reaching new areas, and progressing through the game.

Basic Platformer Elements

1. Static Platforms: 

  • Remains fixed in place.

  • Example: Regular ground or floors.

2. Moving Platforms: 

  • Moves in a set pattern (horizontally, vertically, diagonally).

  • Example: Elevators or conveyor belts.

3. Falling Platforms

  • Collapses or disappears shortly after being stepped on.

  • Example: Crumbling bridges.

4. Vanishing Platforms

  • Appears and disappears at intervals in sequence.

  • Example: Timed platforms.

5. Spring/Bounce Platforms

  • Launches the player to the air when jumped on.

  • Example: Trampolines or jump pads.

6. Slippery Platforms

  • Reduced friction causes the player to slide.

  • Example: Ice surfaces.

7. Breakable Platforms

  • Shatters or collapses after stepped or jumped on.

  • Example: Cracked tiles that break after use.

8. Sticky Platforms

  • Slows the player down or prevent jumping.

  • Example: Slime covered surfaces.

9. Rotating Platforms

  • Spins around a fixed point, requiring precise jumps.

  • Example: Spinning gears or logs.

10. Conveyor Platforms

  • Automatically pushes the player in a direction.

  • Example: Assembly line belts, wind zone.

11. Hazardous Platforms

  • Causes damage or knockback.

  • Example: Electrified or spiked platforms.

12. Floating Platforms

  • Moves dynamically based on physics (buoyancy, swaying, tilting).

  • Example: Rafts or balloons.

13. Reverse Gravity Platforms

  • Flips gravity when stepped on.

  • Example: Ceiling-walking mechanics.

14. Teleporting Platforms

  • Warps the player to another location upon stepping on them.

  • Example: Magic portals.
